dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Denise.
Hi Denise, Walter Thurston. I know it's Saturday afternoon and City Hall's closed up, so I figured this was the number for the weather stuff. Is that right?
That's right, this line's open for storm problems when the offices are closed. What's going on?

Okay. So I manage a few buildings on the island, and I'm standing in the yard of one of them right now, and I've got water coming down off the hill from the next street over. Straight down. It comes right across the grass like a creek.
This is from the storm that came through, Friday into today?

Yeah, the coastal one. It came in Friday and it finally quit this morning, but the water's still pouring down. And the drain on the corner is just sitting there. Nothing's going into it. It's full of leaves and gravel and who knows what.
Okay. Can you give me the address, or the closest cross street?

Hang on, let me, [pause] you know, I grew up down by the harbor, and my father used to say you could tell a storm was a real one by what the water did to the street. Used to watch it run right off the wharf. Anyway. Sorry. You want a location.
Whenever you're ready, Mr. Thurston.

The thing is, I'd rather not get into the exact number on the phone right now, I'm on my cell and I've got one bar. It's the hill above the yard, the drain's at the bottom where the two streets meet. Is that enough for you?
I do need something to send a crew to. Is there a street name for the drain, even just the street it's on?
It's, uh, hold on. [line breaks up] Can you hear me?
You cut out for a second. I lost you after "hold on."

Yeah, the signal here's lousy. I said it's the drain at the bottom of the hill, the one the whole street drains to. I'll be honest, I'm calling because this isn't the first time. Every big rain, same thing, and nobody comes out to clean it.
I hear you. Is the water going into any buildings right now?

Not into mine yet. But it's moving toward the neighbor's garage. It's about, I'd say, ten, twelve feet from the garage door and it's coming along the edge of the driveway. If it keeps up, that garage is going to take water.
Okay, that's important. Is anybody home at the neighbor's, can they put something down at the door?
I knocked, nobody's answering. Car's gone. I've got a couple of sandbags in the truck, so I'm going to throw those at the door after this call.
That's a good idea. And how deep is the water where it's running?
Over the tops of my boots in the low part by the drain. Across the yard it's just a few inches, but it's fast.
Got it. I'm putting this in as an urgent drain blockage with water heading toward a garage. What I need is a street, and I'll get it to the crew on call.

Okay, okay. Look, it's off Memorial Boulevard. That's the best I can do on the phone. Funny, that's where I learned to parallel park, in my uncle's Buick, up and down Memorial Boulevard. Scared the daylights out of the whole block. But I'll tell you, that street I could do in my sleep. This one I can't get anybody to look at.
A Buick, that's a tough one to park. Okay, so it's near Memorial Boulevard. Which side, the water side or toward the hill?
Uphill side. The street above runs along the ridge and everything pours down from there. The drain's at the low spot, right where it hits the yard.

All right. Let me read back what I have. A blocked storm drain at the bottom of a hill near Memorial Boulevard, runoff crossing a yard and heading for a neighbor's garage, after the storm. And you're asking for the drain to be cleaned out. Right?
Yes. Cleaned out, cleared, whatever you call it. I just need somebody with the truck to come pull the junk out of it. I've asked before and it's the same story every time.

I'm sorry about that. Crews are stretched thin right after a storm like this, and there's a lot of calls for drains. But I'll flag this one as active water toward a structure, which should move it up.
I appreciate that. I do. But I'm gonna be honest, I'm tired of hearing it'll get looked at. It never gets looked at until somebody's garage is full of water.
Understood. I can't tell you the exact hour a crew will show, but it goes to the on-call supervisor today. Do you want a call back when it's been assigned?
Yeah, call me back. It's 401-555-0176.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-six. And that's Walter Thurston?
T-H-U-R-S-T-O-N. Yep.
Got it. One more thing. Is the water also going into the street, or only across the yard?
Both. It's coming off the road above, across the yard, and some of it's running along the curb toward the next house. It's all one big sheet.
Okay. Please stay out of the moving water if you can, and keep away from the drain itself. Don't try to pull the grate.
I wasn't going to. I did poke at it with a rake, though. Just the leaves on top. Didn't make a dent.
That's fine, just be careful. If the water starts getting into the garage or a building, call this line right back and tell whoever answers that it's entering a structure.
Will do. And you'll put in that it's repeat? That it's not the first time?
I'll note that you say it backs up every time there's heavy rain, and that you'd like it cleaned.
Good. Because I've watched this for years. Honest to God, the drain's never been touched that I can see.
I've got it in the notes. Anything else you want me to add?
No, that's it. Thanks, Denise. I'm going to go sandbag that garage before it gets worse.
Go ahead. Take care, Mr. Thurston, and stay dry out there.
